title: Stride-aware kernel candidate selector and compact rehash policy for reducing KV fragmentation during interleaved prefill
creator: Ravi Patel
description:
Background: On high-concurrency workloads we observe interleaved prefill and decode waves causing KV page fragmentation and repeated kernel mismatches. Small strides of repeated short sequences push hot tokens into scattered slots, increasing eviction churn and causing the kernel selector to oscillate between narrow and wide kernels. Goal: Reduce fragmentation and oscillation without sacrificing tail latency by introducing a stride-aware kernel candidate selector plus a compact-then-rehash policy for KV pages during prefill windows.

Proposal: 1) Kernel candidate selector: maintain lightweight per-request stride fingerprint (delta of recent key indices) to bias kernel candidate ranking toward kernels that historically colocate the computed KV ranges. This is encoded as a 2-bit stride signature per session and consulted by the scheduler when choosing kernel variants (narrow/wide/tile). 2) Compact rehash policy: when a page's fragmentation score exceeds threshold F (empirically 0.28) and the page has low active decode concurrency, trigger an in-place compaction pass that coalesces contiguous slots then rehashes pointer table with a bounded budget (milliseconds). 3) Prefill smoothing: throttle admitting new prefill waves for tenants that show high stride variance; use backpressure to prefer decode continuity on hot sessions. 4) Graceful fallback: if compaction would exceed time budget or causes increased GPU stalls, fall back to lazy rehash marker and prioritized eviction.

Deliverables: design doc with microbenchmarks, scheduler patches, compaction microkernel, e2e benchmark on long-tail conversational corpus, dashboard panels for fragmentation score and kernel mismatch rate. Acceptance criteria: fragmentation score reduced by >=30% on skewed workloads, 10-15% token-cost reduction from fewer re-prefills, no >5% regression in p99 latency.

Risks & mitigations: compaction can introduce stalls — mitigate with timeboxed compaction and offloaded async compaction on spare SMs where supported. Stride signals may mislead in mixed-traffic — combine with TTL and confidence weights.

Links: design draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Stride+Aware+Kernel+Selector, perf dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv_frag/kv-fragmentation, WIP PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2419
updates: 2026-03-02: Spike complete — measured fragmentation metric (F) and validated threshold 0.28 on sampled fleet traces. Local microbench shows 22% reduction in re-prefill events using naive stride heuristic.

2026-03-04: Prototype kernel selector integrated into candidate ranking layer. Observed oscillation reduction in synthetic interleaved workload but small p50 latency bump (+1.7ms) — investigating prefill smoothing parameters.
2026-03-06: Implemented timeboxed compaction kernel. On Ampere testbed compaction cost ~2.2ms for a 16KB page; introduced async offload path reducing visible stall to ~0.4ms.
2026-03-08: Code review feedback from Marco (serving-runtime) — request to add telemetry for stride-confidence and to make compaction budget configurable per shard. Addressed in PR #2419.

2026-03-10: Canary run started on dedicated pool (tenant subset). Initial results: fragmentation -31%, kernel mismatch rate -18%, p99 latency unchanged within noise. Continuing canary for 72h and monitoring regressions.
notes: Follow-up: add unit tests for stride signature collisions and a simulator to replay mixed-stride traffic.
Product ask: include 'prefill-smoothing' as a knob in console rollout controls to allow customers to tune aggressiveness for latency-sensitive apps.
Operational: add alert if compaction backlog grows >3 per shard to detect pathological compaction loops.
